title: Collections Framework
summary: The Collections Framework gives you List (ordered, duplicates allowed — ArrayList/LinkedList), Set (no duplicates — HashSet/TreeSet), and Map (key-value — HashMap/TreeMap), all built on shared interfaces so you can swap implementations without changing calling code.
example: Reach for LinkedList over ArrayList only when you're doing frequent insert/remove at the head or middle — for anything else, ArrayList's better cache locality wins in practice.
mistakes: Using HashMap from multiple threads without synchronization — it can silently corrupt state, not just throw. Use ConcurrentHashMap instead.
Assuming HashSet/HashMap preserve insertion order — they don't; use LinkedHashSet/LinkedHashMap if order matters.
